record.narrative: The new validation evidence confirms the two remaining high-value in-dataset associations. For H18, KEAP1 loss versus NFE2L2 dependency is registered in the direction of weaker NFE2L2 dependency; the independent validation signed estimate is +0.781, with interval +0.752 to +0.809. The 10% practical threshold for NFE2L2 is about 0.0093, so the validation interval is entirely and far above that threshold. Combined with the discovery estimate +0.796, this strongly supports KEAP1-loss cells having much weaker NFE2L2 dependency in this supplied dataset. I therefore accept and close H18. For H13, MSI-high versus WRN dependency is registered in the direction of stronger WRN dependency, i.e. a more negative WRN score. The newly delivered overall validation signed estimate is +0.771, interval +0.720 to +0.822. The WRN 10% threshold is about 0.0301, so the independent interval is also entirely and overwhelmingly above the practical threshold. This validates the overall MSI-high/WRN association, not only the adenocarcinoma subgroup result already validated in H24. I therefore accept and close H13. The core validated set is now SMARCA4 loss/stronger SMARCA2 dependency, TP53 loss/weaker USP7 dependency, KEAP1 loss/weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and MSI-high/stronger WRN dependency overall and in adenocarcinoma. The most informative unresolved signal is the NF1-loss bypass signal for KRAS dependency. The discovery result in KRAS-wildtype cells was +0.0387, interval +0.0062 to +0.0712, exceeding the KRAS threshold at the point estimate and excluding zero, but the lower bound is below the 10% practical threshold. I keep H67 unresolved and prioritize its registered context refinements plus two new analyses: a specificity interaction to test whether the NF1-loss effect is larger in KRAS-wildtype than KRAS-mutant cells, and a direct KRAS-mutation test in NF1-intact cells to see whether the borderline KRAS effect becomes meaningful when NF1-loss confounding is reduced. The borderline KRAS and EGFR main effects remain unresolved but are deferred rather than accepted; their existing intervals remain compatible with small effects crossing zero and threshold. The TP53-loss/MDM2 effect also remains unresolved but deferred, because the point estimate is small and the confidence interval only partly overlaps the practical threshold. These statements are associations within the supplied dataset and not claims of causality or external generalizability.

record.narrative: The accepted and independently validated core in-dataset associations remain: SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; TP53 loss with much weaker USP7 dependency; KEAP1 loss with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency; and MSI-high with much stronger WRN dependency overall and in adenocarcinoma. The most actionable unresolved signal is the NF1-loss/bypass signal for KRAS dependency. The discovery mean difference among KRAS-wildtype cells was +0.0387, interval +0.0062 to +0.0712, signed toward weaker KRAS dependency. The point estimate exceeds the KRAS 10% practical threshold of about 0.0245 and excludes zero, but the confidence interval is still compatible with subthreshold effects. I therefore registered refinements that test whether the NF1-loss effect persists and is context-specific: whether it is modified by TP53 loss, adenocarcinoma subtype, or screen batch; and whether a direct KRAS-mutation effect becomes clearer when NF1-loss and TP53-loss contexts are removed. I also added a mechanistic pathway check asking whether NF1 loss is associated with weaker RIT1 dependency, a more upstream RAS-pathway gene, which would be consistent with pathway bypass but is not required. Next, I proposed refinements to borderline oncogene hypotheses. For BRAF and ERBB2, the overall tests were not accepted; conditional tests in mutually cleaner genetic contexts may reveal oncogene addiction effects that were diluted by co-alterations. For RIT1, KRAS mutation is expected to reduce dependency on upstream RAS-pathway input, so I registered a weaker-dependency direction. For STAT3, ERBB2 amplification is a plausible activator of STAT3 signaling, with stronger STAT3 dependency expected. For USP7, MYC amplification is a plausible test of deubiquitinase-dependency relationships, though alternative null or opposite directions remain possible. For DHX9, MSI-high is expected to show stronger helicase replication-stress dependency if the accepted WRN effect reflects broader replication stress, but the null is that WRN is the specific helicase dependency. These remain in-dataset association tests, not causal claims or claims of external generalizability.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

The point estimate exceeds the KRAS 10% practical threshold of about 0.0245 and excludes zero, but the confidence interval is still compatible with subthreshold effects. I therefore registered refinements that test whether the NF1-loss effect persists and is context-specific: whether it is modified by TP53 loss, adenocarcinoma subtype, or screen batch; and whether a direct KRAS-mutation effect becomes clearer when NF1-loss and TP53-loss contexts are removed. For STAT3, ERBB2 amplification is a plausible activator of STAT3 signaling, with stronger STAT3 dependency expected. For USP7, MYC amplification is a plausible test of deubiquitinase-dependency relationships, though alternative null or opposite directions remain possible. record.narrative: I selected twelve active, previously untested comparisons that best address the current priorities: resolve the borderline NF1-loss/KRAS-dependency signal, assess whether direct KRAS-mutation effects are masked by co-alterations, revisit mutually cleaner oncogene contexts, and test biologically coherent pathway or replication-stress follow-ups. All returned estimates will be interpreted as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction; positive values support the registered claim and negative values oppose it. Practical mean-difference thresholds are approximately KRAS 0.0245, BRAF 0.0248, ERBB2 0.0260, RIT1 0.0256, STAT3 0.0282, DHX9 0.0250, and MDM2 0.0269, using 10% of the absolute overall outcome mean. H68-H70 test whether the NF1-loss association among KRAS-wildtype cells persists in TP53-intact, EGFR-amplification-intact, and adenocarcinoma contexts, where the registered direction +1 corresponds to weaker KRAS dependency. H71 is the key specificity interaction: with direction -1, a positive signed estimate means the NF1-loss effect is larger in KRAS-wildtype than in KRAS-mutant cells. H72 tests direct KRAS-mutation dependency among NF1-intact cells, assessing whether NF1-loss co-alteration dilutes the direct KRAS mutation effect. H83 tests pathway coherence by asking whether NF1 loss also predicts weaker RIT1 dependency among KRAS-wildtype cells. H77 and H78 revisit BRAF and ERBB2 oncogene dependencies in contexts where a common alternative driver is absent: KRAS-wildtype cells for BRAF and EGFR-amplification-intact cells for ERBB2. H79 and H80 test pathway dependencies: KRAS mutation versus RIT1 dependency and ERBB2 amplification versus STAT3 dependency. H82 tests whether MSI-high predicts stronger DHX9 dependency, a specificity check for the accepted MSI-high/WRN association. H21 resolves the unresolved TP53-loss/MDM2 pathway signal within the largest lineage subtype. These analyses are discovery association tests in the supplied dataset, not causal or external-generality claims.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All estimates below are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive values support the registered claim and negative values oppose it. I used approximate 10% practical thresholds from the absolute overall means: KRAS about 0.0245, BRAF about 0.0248, ERBB2 about 0.0260, RIT1 about 0.0256, STAT3 about 0.0282, DHX9 about 0.0250, and MDM2 about 0.0269. For the NF1-loss/KRAS-dependency signal, H68 is the strongest clean context so far: NF1 loss among KRAS-wildtype and TP53-intact cells has signed estimate +0.0428, interval +0.0048 to +0.0807, indicating weaker KRAS dependency. It excludes zero and exceeds the practical threshold at the point estimate, but the lower bound is still well below the 10% threshold, so it does not establish a clinically meaningful effect. H69 is similar but with lower bound only +0.0011, and H70 in adenocarcinoma crosses zero. H71 suggests context specificity, but the signed interaction +0.0674 has lower bound essentially at zero and relies on a small KRAS-mutant/NF1-loss cell with only 49 observations, so it is not decisive. H72 directly tests KRAS mutation among NF1-intact cells and is near null, +0.0076; it cannot establish a meaningful direct KRAS-dependency effect. H83 does not support coherent pathway bypass through RIT1, +0.0115. Overall, the NF1/KRAS results are biologically coherent and consistently positive in several contexts, but the discovery intervals are too imprecise to assert at least 10% weaker KRAS dependency. I therefore request independent validation for H67, the broader KRAS-wildtype NF1-loss context, because it is the primary unresolved claim and has slightly larger exposure cells than the TP53-intact refinement. If validation supports a precise effect above the KRAS practical threshold, I can accept; if it remains borderline or crosses zero, the NF1/KRAS signal should remain unresolved or be closed. H77 opposes the registered BRAF-dependency direction in KRAS-wildtype cells and the maximum clinically meaningful positive effect is below the BRAF threshold, so reject and close. H78 is essentially null for conditional ERBB2 amplification among EGFR-amplification-intact cells; because the upper bound is only marginally above threshold, I keep it formally unresolved but close further work because there is no meaningful signal to pursue. H79 rejects the KRAS-mutation/RIT1 association because the interval upper bound is below the RIT1 practical threshold. H80 is not decisive for ERBB2-amplification/STAT3: point estimate is below threshold, interval crosses zero but includes possible meaningful effects; I defer it as low priority. H82 does not support MSI-high/DHX9 as a parallel replication-stress dependency and I close it. H21 does not materially clarify TP53-loss/MDM2 in adenocarcinoma: point estimate remains below threshold and interval crosses zero; I defer it because the overall TP53-loss/MDM2 claim already remains borderline. These conclusions remain associations within the supplied dataset, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: Interpreting all estimates as already signed to the registered direction, the newly delivered validation evidence is decisive for the two response-deadline claims and largely closes the main NF1/KRAS frontier. H7, SMARCA4 loss versus stronger SMARCA2 dependency, is confirmed independently: validation signed estimate +0.807, interval +0.777 to +0.838. The practical 10 percent outcome threshold for SMARCA2 is about 0.0415, so the independent interval is far and uniformly above that threshold; combined with discovery, this is a robust in-dataset association and remains accepted and closed. H24, MSI-high versus stronger WRN dependency within adenocarcinoma, is also confirmed: validation signed estimate +0.784, interval +0.727 to +0.840, against a WRN threshold of about 0.0301. It is accepted and closed. The most important new result is H67, NF1 loss versus weaker KRAS dependency among KRAS-wildtype cells. Discovery was positive and excluded zero (+0.0387, +0.0062 to +0.0712), but the independent validation was essentially null (+0.0005, -0.0415 to +0.0425). The validation point estimate is far below the KRAS 10 percent practical threshold of about 0.0245 and provides no independent support for the broad claim. I therefore reject and close H67 as a general KRAS-wildtype association. This does not mathematically exclude a small or highly context-specific effect, but the broad signal discovered earlier is not supported by independent validation and should no longer be prioritized. The TP53-intact refinement H68 remains formally unresolved but deferred and low priority; the associated interaction and refinement claims H73 through H76 are closed. Supported findings in the supplied dataset are the large and repeatedly confirmed associations: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency; KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency; and MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency overall and in adenocarcinoma, with additional support in BRCA2-intact and higher mutation-burden contexts. Negative or unsupported findings include BRAF V600E not showing meaningful BRAF-dependency effects overall or in KRAS-wildtype cells, ERBB2 amplification not supporting meaningful ERBB2 dependency overall or in EGFR-amplification-intact cells, KRAS mutation not supporting weaker RIT1 dependency, TP53 loss not supporting meaningful RPL11 dependency, MSI-high not supporting DHX9 dependency, BRCA2-loss synthetic lethality patterns with WRN or DHX9 not supported, PIK3CA mutation not supporting bypass EGFR dependency, MYC amplification not supporting POLR2A dependency, and RB1 loss not supporting KIF18A dependency. Unresolved uncertainty remains for borderline effects such as EGFR amplification, KRAS mutation, TP53 loss with MDM2, ERBB2 amplification with STAT3, and residual NF1 contexts; these intervals cross zero or remain too imprecise relative to practical thresholds, and they are deferred or closed rather than accepted. The accepted batch interaction H35 should also be read cautiously because its lower confidence bound is well below the 10 percent SMARCA2 threshold despite the controller keeping it accepted. The most informative next analysis is H53, testing the MSI-high and WRN association in lower mutation-burden cells, because it interrogates robustness of one of the few large validated associations rather than chasing the failed NF1/KRAS signal. Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

record.narrative: I selected twelve untested active claims that best balance technical robustness, pathway coherence, and follow-up of accepted findings. H84 and H85 test whether the two largest validated pathway associations survive outside the dominant Avana library: KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency. These are specificity checks for library artifacts rather than new biological mechanisms. H86 and H87 ask whether CDKN2A loss in TP53-intact cells resembles aspects of p53-pathway loss for USP7 and MDM2 dependency. H88-H91 test a PI3K/RTK/RAS bypass family of hypotheses: PTEN loss as a downstream bypass of EGFR or KRAS-WT dependency, BRAF V600E as a bypass of RIT1 among KRAS-WT cells, and ERBB2 amplification as an upstream activator that could increase RIT1 dependency. H92 and H93 test broad STAT3 predictors, SMAD4 loss and STK11 loss. H94 tests a MYC association with the mitotic gene KIF18A. H53 is included instead of the more speculative MYC/TMED10 proposal because it directly interrogates the accepted MSI-high/WRN association in lower mutation-burden cells and can reveal whether the WRN effect is robust or mutation-burden dependent. All requested outputs will be interpreted as already signed to the registered direction: positive values support the registered claim, negative values oppose it. Practical 10 percent thresholds are roughly USP7 0.0093, NFE2L2 0.0093, MDM2 0.0269, EGFR 0.0250, KRAS 0.0245, RIT1 0.0256, STAT3 0.0282, KIF18A 0.0256, and WRN 0.0301. I will accept only when the direction and interval support an effect at or above the outcome-specific threshold; borderline intervals crossing zero or including subthreshold effects will remain unresolved or be closed if there is no informative signal. These remain associations in the supplied dataset, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

I used practical 10% effect-size benchmarks from the absolute outcome means: NFE2L2 and USP7 about 0.0093, MDM2 about 0.0269, EGFR about 0.0250, KRAS about 0.0245, RIT1 about 0.0256, STAT3 about 0.0282, and KIF18A about 0.0256. These are far above the respective 10% thresholds and support the effects outside the dominant library, although they remain in-dataset associations. H86 does not support CDKN2A loss phenocopying TP53-loss-like weaker USP7 dependency among TP53-intact cells: point -0.0028, interval -0.0251 to +0.0195. The interval still includes small positive effects above the very small USP7 threshold, so I keep it formally unresolved but close further work as unpromising. H87 is not merely null; it strongly opposes the registered hypothesis that CDKN2A loss in TP53-intact cells gives weaker MDM2 dependency. I reject the registered direction and close it, while proposing a new reversed claim because this opposite effect is clinically meaningful in magnitude. Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

expectation

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: All estimates are interpreted as already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive values support the registered claim and negative values oppose it. I used approximately 10% practical thresholds from the absolute outcome means, for example KRAS about 0.0245, RIT1 about 0.0256, WRN about 0.0301, MDM2 about 0.0269, USP7 about 0.0093, and NFE2L2 about 0.0093. H13 remains accepted: MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency overall, discovery +0.790, interval +0.760 to +0.819, and independent validation +0.771, interval +0.720 to +0.822, far above the WRN threshold. H90 is rejected and closed: BRAF V600E among KRAS-wildtype cells had only borderline discovery for weaker RIT1 dependency, discovery +0.013, interval -0.021 to +0.047, and independent validation was near null and on the opposite side of the registered direction, validation -0.007, interval -0.056 to +0.041; although the wide adjusted interval still includes possible positive effects, the independent estimate provides no support for a clinically meaningful weaker-RIT1 effect. H49 is rejected and closed: KRAS mutation among TP53-intact cells was near null on validation for stronger KRAS dependency, validation +0.001, interval -0.028 to +0.030, with a point estimate far below the KRAS 10% threshold and a lower bound below zero; discovery alone was also below threshold. I reassessed H96 as an accepted in-dataset association: CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells is associated with much stronger MDM2 dependency, signed discovery +0.119, interval +0.079 to +0.158, well above the MDM2 threshold. This reverses the original H87 hypothesis and is the most informative new finding, but it remains active pending independent validation or technical robustness checks. Overall supported findings in the supplied dataset include SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, independently validated; TP53 loss with much weaker USP7 dependency, independently validated and supported outside the dominant Avana library; KEAP1 loss with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, independently validated and supported outside Avana; and MSI-high with much stronger WRN dependency overall and in adenocarcinoma, with additional support in higher mutation-burden and BRCA2-intact contexts. Negative or unsupported findings include NF1-loss as a broad KRAS-wildtype bypass, because validation was null; BRAF V600E with meaningful BRAF dependency; KRAS mutation with stronger KRAS dependency in TP53-intact cells; BRAF V600E with weaker RIT1 dependency among KRAS-wildtype cells; ERBB2 amplification with meaningful ERBB2 or RIT1 dependency; KRAS mutation with weaker RIT1 dependency; PTEN loss with EGFR or KRAS-wildtype bypass; PIK3CA mutation with EGFR bypass; MSI-high with DHX9 dependency; BRCA2-loss synthetic-lethality patterns for WRN or DHX9; MYC amplification with POLR2A dependency; RB1 loss with KIF18A dependency; TP53 loss with RPL11 dependency; and STK11 loss with NFE2L2 dependency overall. Unresolved uncertainty remains for borderline claims such as EGFR amplification, broad KRAS mutation, TP53 loss with MDM2, ERBB2 amplification with STAT3, several broad STAT3 and MYC predictors, and the SMARCA4 batch interaction H35, where the lower confidence bound remains below the practical 10% benchmark. The most informative next analysis is independent validation or technical and subgroup robustness of H96, CDKN2A loss in TP53-intact cells with stronger MDM2 dependency, including the proposed non-Avana and adenocarcinoma checks. Additional useful follow-up is the proposed conditional STK11-loss test among KEAP1-intact cells for NFE2L2 and the PIK3CA-mutation test among KRAS-wildtype cells. All conclusions are associations within the supplied dataset, not causal claims or claims of external generalizability.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: Current priority is to extend and localize the newly accepted CDKN2A-loss finding and to complete biological/technical characterization of the core accepted associations. Estimates will be interpreted as already signed to the registered direction; positive values support the registered claim. Practical 10% thresholds remain approximately USP7 0.0093, MDM2 0.0269, KRAS 0.0245, and RIT1 0.0256. First, I test TP53 loss and weaker USP7 dependency among KEAP1-intact cells. The complementary KEAP1-loss stratum was accepted (H43), and the overall TP53/USP7 association was independently validated (H12), so the KEAP1-intact complement is needed to establish that the effect is not restricted to or driven only by KEAP1-loss cells. Second, I refine H96, the strongest new signal: CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells is associated with much stronger MDM2 dependency. A low 9p21 copy-number stratum is a plausible proxy for CDKN2A/p14ARF locus deletion, so I test whether the stronger MDM2 dependency is concentrated there. I also test whether MTAP loss, often co-deleted with CDKN2A, further distinguishes CDKN2A-loss cells, because locus co-deletion may indicate a more complete functional disruption of the 9p21 regulatory module. These are mechanistic refinements, not external causal claims. Third, I open two coherent bypass-oriented hypotheses that have not yet been tested: STK11 loss in KRAS-mutant cells may reduce dependence on mutant KRAS through alternative growth/survival signaling, and PIK3CA mutation in KRAS-wildtype cells may bypass upstream RIT1 input by activating downstream PI3K signaling. I register the latter as weaker RIT1 dependency. These proposals are intended to be analyzed alongside H97-H100, which already test non-Avana and adenocarcinoma robustness for the MDM2/CDKN2A signal and PIK3CA/KRAS-WT dependency. If H97 and H98 remain positive, the next appraise stage should strongly consider independent validation of H96 or the most biologically specific refinement. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset; they are not causal or externally generalizable until independently supported.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative:
I selected twelve previously registered, currently active, and not-yet-tested comparisons that most directly refine the strongest accepted associations and the new CDKN2A/MDM2 finding. All returned estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive values support the registered claim and negative values oppose it. The approximate practical 10% thresholds remain USP7 and NFE2L2 about 0.0093, MDM2 about 0.0269, KRAS about 0.0245, and RIT1 about 0.0256.

First, I prioritize H96 follow-up: H97 tests the CDKN2A-loss/stronger-MDM2 association among TP53-intact cells using non-Avana screens, and H98 tests the same association within adenocarcinoma. H102 asks whether the effect is concentrated in a low-9p21 copy-number stratum, a plausible deletion proxy for the CDKN2A/p14ARF locus. H103 tests whether MTAP co-loss among CDKN2A-loss, TP53-intact cells further strengthens MDM2 dependency, which would support broader 9p21 regulatory-module involvement rather than an isolated predictor artifact. If H97 and H98 remain positive, this provides the technical and lineage robustness needed to consider independent validation of H96.

Second, I complete the accepted TP53/USP7 story. H43 accepted TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency within KEAP1-loss cells; H101 now tests the complementary KEAP1-intact stratum. A positive result would indicate the association is not confined to KEAP1-loss cells and supports independence of the TP53/USP7 signal from KEAP1 status.

Third, I test complement/conditional robustness for the accepted KEAP1/NFE2L2 association. H40 tests KEAP1-loss effect in TP53-intact cells, H41 in KRAS-mutant cells, and H54 in EGFR-amplification-negative cells. These are not intended as separate causal mechanisms but as stability checks across orthogonal genomic contexts. H99 asks a narrower conditional question: whether STK11 loss associates with weaker NFE2L2 dependency among KEAP1-intact cells, since the unconditional STK11/NFE2L2 test was not supported.

Finally, I test three coherent bypass-oriented hypotheses that had not yet been analyzed: H100 asks whether PIK3CA mutation reduces KRAS dependency among KRAS-wildtype cells; H104 asks whether STK11 loss reduces KRAS dependency among KRAS-mutant cells; and H105 asks whether PIK3CA mutation reduces RIT1 dependency among KRAS-wildtype cells. These are all registered as weaker-dependency hypotheses, so positive signed estimates support reduced dependency. I will interpret intervals against the practical 10% benchmark: accept only when the evidence supports an effect at or above threshold, close clearly null or subthreshold claims, and keep borderline effects unresolved only if follow-up is justified.

record.narrative: All estimates are interpreted as already signed to the registered direction, so positive values support the registered hypothesis and negative values oppose it. Practical 10 percent thresholds used here are approximately USP7 0.0093, NFE2L2 0.0093, MDM2 0.0269, KRAS 0.0245, and RIT1 0.0256. H101 completes the TP53 loss and USP7 story by testing the KEAP1-intact complement. Its signed estimate is +0.804, interval +0.782 to +0.827, with cell sizes 321 and 1286; this is enormously above the USP7 threshold and, together with validated H12, accepted H25, H43, and non-Avana H85, supports the association independently of KEAP1 status. I accept and close H101. H40, H41, and H54 are complement robustness checks for KEAP1 loss and weaker NFE2L2 dependency in TP53-intact, KRAS-mutant, and EGFR-amplification-negative cells. Their signed estimates are +0.792, +0.805, and +0.793, with lower bounds +0.770, +0.767, and +0.771 respectively. These are far above the NFE2L2 threshold and are close to the previously validated effect size, so I accept and close all three. The CDKN2A-loss and MDM2 signal receives strong within-dataset robustness support. H97, the non-Avana TP53-intact subset, has signed estimate +0.130 and lower bound +0.040, above the MDM2 threshold despite small cell sizes 39 and 153. H98, the adenocarcinoma TP53-intact subset, has +0.103 and lower bound +0.057. H102, the low-9p21 copy-number stratum, has +0.112 and lower bound +0.062. Because the lower bounds all exceed the practical 10 percent threshold, I accept these as supportive in-dataset associations and close them. However, they are all subsets of the same supplied dataset, so independent validation is still needed for the main H96 claim; I request validation for H96. H103 tests MTAP co-loss within CDKN2A-loss TP53-intact cells. Its signed estimate is +0.065, interval -0.034 to +0.164. The interval crosses zero, includes subthreshold effects, and is very wide; the evidence is too imprecise to distinguish a clinically meaningful MTAP co-deletion effect from no effect. I keep H103 unresolved and deferred, and register broader MTAP comparisons as targeted follow-up proposals. The remaining new bypass tests are not supported. H99, STK11 loss among KEAP1-intact cells for weaker NFE2L2 dependency, is essentially null: -0.0017, interval -0.023 to +0.0195, so I reject and close it. H100, PIK3CA mutation for weaker KRAS dependency among KRAS-wildtype cells, is near null with opposite-signed point estimate, -0.0008, interval -0.026 to +0.0246; I reject and close it. H104, STK11 loss among KRAS-mutant cells for weaker KRAS dependency, has negative point estimate -0.0139 and interval -0.053 to +0.0256; the upper bound is only marginally around the KRAS threshold and the interval is dominated by zero and opposite-signed values, so there is no meaningful support and I reject and close it. H105, PIK3CA mutation for weaker RIT1 dependency among KRAS-wildtype cells, is near null with upper bound +0.0187 below the RIT1 threshold, so I reject and close it. record.narrative: Independent validation changes the scientific picture materially. For H96, the claim that CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells is associated with much stronger MDM2 dependency is now independently validated. The signed estimate for the registered direction is +0.122 in the validation split, with an independent 95% interval from +0.064 to +0.180 and cell sizes 321 and 1274. Using the absolute mean of dependency_MDM2 as the denominator for the 10 percent practical benchmark, the threshold is about 0.0269, so even the adjusted lower bound is more than two-fold above the clinically meaningful benchmark. Because positive signed values correspond, for this outcome, to a more negative raw CRISPR dependency score, CDKN2A-loss cells appear to have stronger MDM2 dependency when TP53 is intact. This is now one of the strongest supported associations in the supplied dataset. It remains an association in the supplied validation split, not evidence of causality or external biological generalizability. The earlier discovery and subgroup robustness checks (non-Avana, adenocarcinoma, and low-9p21 copy-number stratum) align with the same direction and magnitude. H67, NF1 loss among KRAS-wildtype cells, is explicitly rejected and closed. Its discovery estimate was borderline and not robust across uncertainty, and the independent validation estimate is essentially null: +0.0005 with an interval from -0.042 to +0.043. This does not support NF1 loss as a meaningful bypass or modifier of KRAS dependency in the tested KRAS-wildtype population. Therefore the main validated supported claims are SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, TP53 loss with much weaker USP7 dependency, KEAP1 loss with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, MSI-high with much stronger WRN dependency, and CDKN2A loss with much stronger MDM2 dependency specifically in TP53-intact cells. The next most informative analyses should localize the CDKN2A/MDM2 finding rather than broaden into low-prior predictors. I propose a direct TP53-loss complement mean difference and an interaction contrast by TP53-loss status. If CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in TP53-intact cells but not in TP53-loss cells, that would support pathway specificity through the intact p53 regulatory axis, though still only as an association. The active MTAP-loss proposals H106 and H107 are also worth prioritizing because they test whether nearby 9p21 co-deletion markers add to the CDKN2A/MDM2 signal. H42 remains useful for completing KEAP1/NFE2L2 robustness in the EGFR-amplification context. Broad EGFR, KRAS, MYC, STAT3, and RIT1 bypass screens are lower priority unless they become mechanistically connected to these validated signals.

expectation

and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative:
I registered seven refinements that together should complete the most informative set of currently active tests when combined with H42, H106, H107, H108, and H109. All returned estimates will be interpreted as already signed to the registered direction. For the new direction -1 hypotheses, a positive signed value supports the registered claim: for MDM2 or SMARCA2, a negative raw exposed-minus-comparator difference means cells in the exposed group have a more negative, hence stronger, dependency score. For interaction contrasts with direction -1, a positive signed value means the exposed-comparator effect is more negative in the indicated subgroup than in its complement. The main practical thresholds remain approximately MDM2 0.0269 and SMARCA2 0.0415, corresponding to 10 percent of the absolute outcome means.

The primary focus remains localization and robustness of the validated CDKN2A-loss signal in TP53-intact cells (H96), not a causal claim. First, I register the effect within screen_batch batch_a to assess technical batch robustness. A positive signed result would indicate that the stronger MDM2 dependency associated with CDKN2A loss is present in the largest screen batch; a null or reversed result would raise a batch-specific technical concern. Second, I test the same association in a high-9p21-copy stratum and register a low-versus-high 9p21 interaction. H102 found support in the low-copy stratum, but that alone cannot determine whether CDKN2A loss matters generally or only in cells with nearby locus deletion. If the high-copy effect remains substantial and the interaction is near null, the CDKN2A association is not driven exclusively by low 9p21 copy number. If the interaction is strongly positive, the effect may be concentrated in deletion-like genomic contexts. Third, I test CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact and MTAP-intact cells, and register an MTAP-loss interaction. Because MTAP is often co-deleted with CDKN2A, persistence of the CDKN2A effect when MTAP is intact would argue against the effect being purely a marker of broader 9p21 co-deletion. A strong MTAP-loss interaction would support a locus-co-deletion modifier. The active broad MTAP H106 and CDKN2A-intact MTAP H107, plus the active TP53-loss complement H108 and TP53-loss interaction H109, complete this localization.

I also add two comparisons that test whether the accepted synthetic-lethality pattern is pathway-specific rather than a generic predictor effect. First, SMARCA4 loss is tested among TP53-loss cells for stronger SMARCA2 dependency. This checks whether the validated SMARCA4 synthetic lethality remains in the p53-disrupted context, where the TP53/USP7 and CDKN2A/MDM2 effects are particularly relevant. Second, CDKN2A loss is tested against SMARCA2 dependency among TP53-intact cells. This is a specificity control for H96: if CDKN2A loss produces a similarly large change in SMARCA2, the MDM2 association could partly reflect a shared genomic or synthetic-lethality confounder rather than a pathway-selective signal. A null or small SMARCA2 result, together with the large MDM2 result, would support MDM2-specificity. These remain association tests in the supplied data, not causal or generalizable mechanisms. The active H42 KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 test in EGFR-amplification-positive cells remains high priority for completing the validated oxidative-stress pathway robustness set.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct

expectation

record.narrative: I request the complete current active analysis queue: H42 plus H106-H116. This prioritizes mechanistic localization of the independently validated CDKN2A-loss/stronger-MDM2 association in TP53-intact cells, while also completing KEAP1/NFE2L2 robustness and adding pathway-specificity controls. Estimates will be interpreted as already signed to registered directions: for direction -1, positive means stronger dependency; for direction +1, positive means weaker dependency. Practical 10% thresholds are approximately MDM2 0.0269, SMARCA2 0.0415, USP7/NFE2L2 0.0093, and WRN 0.0301. H42 tests KEAP1 loss and weaker NFE2L2 dependency in EGFR-amplification-positive cells, completing the oxidative-stress pathway robustness set after accepted TP53-intact, KRAS-mutant, and EGFR-negative contexts. H106-H114 test nearby 9p21/MTAP co-deletion context: whether MTAP loss itself predicts stronger MDM2 dependency, whether it does so absent CDKN2A loss, and whether CDKN2A-loss MDM2 effects persist when MTAP is intact or differ by MTAP status. H108-H109 test the TP53-loss complement and interaction, which are critical for pathway specificity: if CDKN2A loss affects MDM2 only when TP53 is intact, this supports p53-axis specificity rather than a generic copy-number or synthetic-lethality effect. H110-H112 assess technical and genomic localizability: batch_a robustness, high-9p21-copy stratum, and low-versus-high 9p21 interaction. H115 tests whether the strong SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 synthetic-lethality association persists among TP53-loss cells, while H116 tests whether CDKN2A loss also strongly perturbs SMARCA2 among TP53-intact cells, a specificity control for whether the CDKN2A-MDM2 signal is pathway-selective. These are all in-dataset association/localization analyses; acceptance would not establish causality or external generalizability.
